question.problem: The lifetime of a certain type of electrical switch varies continuously. Lifetime of different switches of this type are independent, and switches replacements have a constant average rate of one every $2$ years. Determine the probability that a switch fails between the first and the second year. Round your answer to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Since the lifetime of the switches varies continuously, lifetimes of different switches are independent, and switches replacements have a constant average rate, we can model the lifetime of a switch using the exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ be the lifetime, in years, of a random electrical switch. The lifetime can be modeled as an exponential random variable. Since switches are replaced every $2$ years on average, the rate is $\lambda =\frac{1}{2},$ and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{2}).
$$

In this case, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a switch fails between the first and the second year is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<X<2) & ={\int }_{1}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-x/2}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-{e}^{-1}+{e}^{-1/2} \\  & ≈0.2387\end{aligned}
$$
